passage: The rain had trapped everyone under the bus shelter, and the bus was late. Hansa, five, had discovered the concrete step at the edge. She stood on it, bent her knees, and jumped down with both feet. Splash! "I did it! Rukmini Masi, look!" She climbed back up. Jump. "Again!" Up. Jump. "Again!" Her frock was soaked at the hem. Masi held the umbrella over the step and counted each jump out loud. By the time the bus came, Hansa had jumped nineteen times, and she climbed on grinning, still bending her knees.

qa.q: How many times had Hansa jumped by the time the bus came?
qa.a: Hansa had jumped nineteen times.

qa.q: Why did Hansa keep shouting 'Again!'?
qa.a: Each jump made her feel able and proud, and that good feeling made her want to do it over and over 😊.

qa.q: What did Rukmini Masi choose to do in the rain, and why did it help?
qa.a: She held the umbrella over the step and counted each jump, making Hansa's new skill feel seen and safe to practise.

qa.q: What might the other people at the shelter think, watching Hansa?
qa.a: They might smile at the small girl's delight, which makes the late bus and the rain a little easier to bear.

grounding: A five-year-old proudly jumps off a step in the rain and asks to do it again and again.

passage: In their Kochi apartment building, Elizabeth aunty from the flat next door was blowing up balloons for her son's birthday. Salma sat beside her on the stairs, watching. "Can I tie one?" Elizabeth aunty showed her: wrap, tuck, pull. The first balloon whooshed out of Salma's fingers and flew down the stairs. The second one too. On the third try, the knot held. Salma held it up with both hands, eyes huge. "I tied it! Me!" She grabbed another balloon. "Blow this one! I'll tie!" She tied eleven balloons that afternoon, each a bit lopsided, and after every single knot she said, "Look, aunty. Look."

qa.q: How many balloons did Salma tie that afternoon?
qa.a: She tied eleven balloons, each a bit lopsided.

qa.q: What does 'I tied it! Me!' with huge eyes tell us about how Salma felt?
qa.a: She felt amazed and proud of her new skill, and that pride made her want to tie every balloon.

qa.q: What choice did Elizabeth aunty make after the first two balloons flew away?
qa.a: She let Salma keep trying instead of taking over, so Salma could feel the knot finally hold on her own.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth aunty feel hearing 'Look, aunty. Look.' after every knot?
qa.a: She may feel warm and a little amused, sharing a child's pride in something grown-ups do without thinking 😊.

grounding: A small girl learns to tie a balloon knot and proudly repeats it again and again.

passage:
'Mummy! Mummy! Watch!' Deepak stood on the second stair, knees bent.
'I'm watching,' said Mahima, drying her hands on a towel.
He jumped. Thump! Both feet on the floor. He wobbled, but didn't fall.
'I did it! From the SECOND one!'
'You did! Wah!'
'Again!' He climbed back up. 'Watch again!'
Thump!
Papa came out of the bathroom. 'What's all the noise?'
'Papa, I can jump from the second stair! Watch me!'
'Hmm, show me.'
Thump! Deepak threw his arms up. 'Now the third one?'
Mahima laughed. 'Tomorrow, the third one. Today you've done the second twenty times.'

qa.q: Which stair did Deepak jump from?
qa.a: From the second stair, landing with both feet on the floor.

qa.q: Why did Deepak want Papa to watch too?
qa.a: He was so proud of his new jump that he wanted everyone to see it and share how able he felt.

qa.q: What did Mahima decide about the third stair, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: She said 'Tomorrow, the third one', keeping his excitement alive while letting him enjoy mastering the second step first.

qa.q: What is it like for Mahima to hear 'Again!' so many times?
qa.a: Mahima may feel a bit tired of watching but also delighted, seeing how proud her son is of his new jump.

grounding: A little boy proudly jumps from the second stair and asks his parents to watch again and again.

passage:
Preschool note, Friday. Neelam.
Today Gargi (5) tied her first proper knot on the lacing card, a real double knot. She held it up to me with both hands. 'Look! Look! I did it!'
Then she pulled it loose and did it again. And again. Seven times, counting out loud. Each time she checked my face.
She asked to take a shoelace home 'to practise on Papa's shoes'. I gave her one.
Plan for next week: bows. She's ready, and she wants it.

qa.q: How many times did Gargi tie the knot?
qa.a: Seven times, counting out loud.

qa.q: Why did Gargi keep untying and retying the knot?
qa.a: She felt proud of being able to do it and wanted that feeling again and again; each success made her want to try more.

qa.q: What choice did Neelam make that fed Gargi's eagerness?
qa.a: Neelam gave her a shoelace to take home and planned bows for next week, building on her pride with the next small challenge.

qa.q: How might Papa feel when Gargi practises knots on his shoes?
qa.a: Papa may be amused and proud, perhaps finding his shoes knotted, but seeing how excited Gargi is to show a new skill.

grounding: A teacher notes a young child who proudly ties her first knot and wants to do it again and again.

passage:
At the ghat steps near the temple in their small town, Kamal stood on the second step, knees bent, fists tight. The step below looked very far away.
'Jump, Kamal!' called his didi, Sukanya, holding the flower basket.
He jumped. He landed on both feet, wobbled, and didn't fall. His mouth fell open. 'Didi! I jumped the big one!'
Before she could answer, he climbed back up. Jump. Again. Again. Each time he shouted, 'Did you see?'
Sukanya put the basket down and counted for him. By eleven, the old priest sweeping the steps was counting too.

qa.q: Who was sweeping the steps?
qa.a: The old priest.

qa.q: How can you tell Kamal felt proud after the first jump?
qa.a: His mouth fell open, he shouted 'I jumped the big one!' and climbed straight back up to do it again.

qa.q: What choice of Sukanya's helped Kamal keep practising?
qa.a: She put the basket down and counted his jumps, noticing each one, which fed his pride and his effort.

qa.q: What might the old priest have enjoyed in joining the counting?
qa.a: The priest probably enjoyed Kamal's delight and wanted to share in it, adding another pair of eyes to his proud jumps. 🙂

grounding: A young child proudly jumps a big step and wants to do it again and again, the feeling of being able driving him on.
